title: Degree formula for the local Frobenius
statement:
Use the global finite-field datum and coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], so $A=A_{E,n}$, $X_0$ is separated
of finite type over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$.
Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. Let $x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point of
positive degree $d_x=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$, let $m\geq1$ be an integer
divisible by $d_x$, and let $x_m\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^{d_x}})$ be a
point above $x$. Write $\bar x$ for its geometric lift to $X$ and put
$F_x=F_{x_m,d_x}$, the one-circuit local Frobenius of
[def-trf-frobenius-operators], well defined up to conjugation by
[lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy]. Then for every
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$, with geometric lift $\bar y$,
$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr)
=
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_x^{\,m/d_x}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
$$
in $A$, where $\operatorname{tr}_A$ is the categorical trace of
[def-trf-categorical-trace].

proof.text:
*Step 1: the fixed-point transport cocycle.* Put $d=d_x$, write $m=rd$ with $r\geq1$, and let $z_j$ be the level-$j$ rational point with geometric lift $\bar x$ whenever $j>0$ and $d\mid j$. Clause (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] gives $\Phi^j\bar x=\bar x$. Apply [lem-trf-fixed-point-stalk-transport-cocycle] with $z=\bar x$ and with $P_j=L(g_\gamma^j)^*$. Its coefficient hypotheses are exactly those of the item. On the underlying complex $K$, its $t_{j,K}$ is $\tau_{z_j,j}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]: both are the fixed-point composition identification followed by the same specified $\kappa^{(j)}$. Thus, under the specified $P_{a+b}\cong P_aP_b$ comparison,
$$t_{a+b,K}=t_{a,P_bK}\circ t_{b,K}$$
for positive multiples $a,b$ of $d$. The cited lemma also supplies naturality in the coefficient complex, with no Weil structure or perfectness needed for these transport identities.

proof.text:
*Step 3: changing the lift and taking traces.* Given $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ above $x$, clause (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] gives $0\leq i<d$ with $\bar y=G^i(\bar x)=g_\gamma^i\circ\bar x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^i),\quad\sigma(c)=c^q$. Its clauses (2) and (3) supply an isomorphism $T_i:K_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\bar x}$ and
$$
F_{y,m}=T_i^{-1}\circ F_{z_m,m}\circ T_i
=T_i^{-1}\circ F_x^r\circ T_i.
$$
For $i=0$ take $T_0=1$; no undefined $\varphi^{[0]}$ is needed. Multiplying the displayed equality on the left by $T_i$ gives $T_i\circ F_{y,m}=F_x^r\circ T_i$. The stalk assertion of [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] puts both $K_{\bar y}$ and $K_{\bar x}$ in the perfect-complex category $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$: its hypothesis holds because the coefficient conventions give a separated finite-type structure map and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Apply clause (1) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] with $P_1=K_{\bar y}$, $P_2=K_{\bar x}$, $w=T_i$, $v_1=F_{y,m}$ and $v_2=F_x^r$. This gives the asserted trace equality, since $r=m/d_x$.

split_report.summary: Repair of the dedicated Q23 re-split handoff: extracted the naturality and composition law of fixed-point stalk transports into one statement-only node. Retained the explicit operator calculation and positive-exponent induction, then the existing conjugacy/perfect-trace argument. Corrected the description of the lift orbit to include source reparametrization as required by the current conjugacy statement. Statement, statement dependencies, Lean audit and inherited source metadata unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 proof Step 1: new fixed-point-stalk-transport-cocycle supplies the hidden comparison lemma; item steps 1 and 2 apply it and perform the operator calculation and induction. Item step 3 retains blueprint Step 2, using the correctly reparametrized lift orbit.

tool_uses.why: The blueprint proof explicitly uses the cocycle of iterated Weil maps to factor the operator; the proper-global unit has no separate cocycle theorem.
Only its geometric-stalk perfectness clause is used to check the domain of categorical trace; no statement of the proper-global unit supplies it.
The blueprint proof explicitly uses categorical-trace conjugacy invariance after changing the lift; the proper-global unit has no separate trace-invariance theorem.
